- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.2) and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 3–8% to match true decline.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3–5 day moving average before forecasting to reduce overshoot.
- When true price rises sharply after a dip, model often lags; add 1–2 days of lagged price momentum to forecast if sentiment turns positive.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.6) and price is trending, model tends to overfit recent noise; use 10-day rolling mean as baseline for correction.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-period momentum; weight final 7–10 days of history 2x more heavily in smoothing.
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., +0.4 → -0.4 → +0.4), model undercorrects; apply mean reversion to forecast toward 30-day average of prior 10 days.
